rubrics.justification: Accurately identifies a good-quality blastocyst with reassuring ICM and acceptable/good TE, and appropriately notes limits of judging from a single still image. Minor issue: it questions 3AA vs 4AA based on the written description rather than sticking strictly to the provided lab grade/image.

Comprehensively integrates age, tubal factor diagnosis, ovarian reserve markers, stimulation response, semen quality, endometrial thickness, prior cycle history, and lifestyle with embryo quality and prognosis.

Reasoning is logical and well structured, with conclusions generally supported by morphology and clinical context. Slight limitation: implantation/live birth estimates are somewhat broad and depend on assumptions not fully specified.

Recommendations are well aligned with Gardner grading principles, standard IVF prognostic counseling, emphasis on eSET in a young good-prognosis patient, and appropriate caution regarding hydrosalpinx and selective rather than routine PGT-A at age 30.

Provides clear practical next steps including eSET, confirming hydrosalpinx status, standard luteal support, and contingency planning after failure. Useful and nuanced, though some recommendations remain general rather than protocol-specific.
